lines.text: You have never touched anything. Not once, in your entire life.
Not your phone. Not your chair. Not the people you love. Let me show you.
Press a finger on a table. Now zoom in. Past the skin cells. Past the molecules. Down to the atoms.
An atom is almost entirely empty. If its nucleus were a grain of sand, the atom would be a football stadium.
The atoms in your finger and the table never meet. Their electron clouds push each other away.
That push is what you feel as solid. You're always hovering, a billionth of a meter above everything you've ever touched.
It's electromagnetism, plus a quantum rule: two electrons can never share the same state.
Squeeze out all the empty space, and all eight billion humans on Earth would fit inside a sugar cube.
Solid isn't stuff. It's a force. So what else have you been so sure about?
Watch again, and try to find where your finger actually touches.
